notes: The previous boot-blocking crash persists: the linked firmware still resolves dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 to esp-dsp's misaligned-instruction assembly (objdump/addr2line evidence + the functional log's fault address).
The new app_dsp_shim archive is not linked because app_dsp_shim dsp is declared PRIV_REQUIRES but no file in the component references it, so --as-needed drops it.

other app_dsp_shim details once linked: the shim's implementation lacks the 4-byte alignment guard/rescale of esp-dsp's C version, and nothing names it on any other symbol. Even so, once the shim is linked, the crash is expected to vanish; adding anything else in esp-dsp that uses a hardware-loop kernel would need a similar check.

peripherals.driver: app_audio (AFE + MultiNet) — currently crashes in the front end

findings.description: The dmsp shim does not take effect: the built firmware still links esp-dsp's `dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4.S.obj` and the functional log faults at that exact symbol. Cause: app_dsp_shim is listed in app_audio's PRIV_REQUIRES but no file in app_audio #includes or calls anything from it, so the static archive is never pulled in; the linker sees no object and esp-dsp's assembly member is still the one that satisfies the prebuilt esp-sr reference. The CMakeLists comment ("components are processed in dependency order … the linker resolves it here") is not how static linking works — an archive member is only pulled in by an unresolved symbol.
findings.evidence: firmware/build/zerocode_ai_firmware.map:1627/96828 `dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 esp-idf/espressif__esp-dsp/libespressif__esp-dsp.a(dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4.S.obj)` with no libapp_dsp_shim.a entry anywhere; app_dsp_shim/CMakeLists.txt:1-12 (no WHOLE_ARCHIVE, no reference); app_audio/CMakeLists.txt:19 (PRIV_REQUIRES only); artifacts/device.log: backtrace #0 `dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 () at managed_components/espressif__esp-dsp/modules/dotprod/float/dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4.S:52`.
findings.failureScenario: Boot the flashed image: app_audio_init starts the AFE, the first wake-word feature frame calls dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4, which is still the assembly kernel with the `esp.lp.setup` instruction, the emulator (and presumably the silicon) takes an instruction-misaligned trap and the panel aborts before display, web, MQTT and the console — every spec feature remains unreachable, exactly as the functional report describes.
findings.suggestedChange: Force the shim's member into the link, e.g. by making it a name-colliding shared dependency listed before esp-dsp with a reference from app_audio, marking the component WHOLE_ARCHIVE (or the file a linker-enforced OBJECT library), or renaming the component to something esp-sr's prebuilt archive itself depends on so the archive is always searched before esp-dsp; then confirm in the map that the symbol resolves to libapp_dsp_shim.a and the image no longer contains dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4.S.obj.

findings.description: The shim's arithmetic is a plain C accumulation while esp-dsp's C implementation (dsps_dotprod_f32_ansi) applies a 4-sample alignment guard and partial-vector handling; once the symbol is linked from the shim, feature extraction will differ in rounding from every reference build.
findings.failureScenario: Wake-word detection thresholds tuned against esp-dsp's C implementation may be slightly different (rare false negatives), and results differ between the shim and any code path that uses dsps_dotprod_f32_ansi directly (the map shows dsps_sqrt_f32_ansi referenced by esp-sr, so mixed references are already a pattern).
findings.suggestedChange: Reuse esp-dsp's own ANSI implementation body (guarded with the same alignment check) rather than a simplified loop, so the behaviour is identical on every path.
